Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround. We have a few people who want to join next week: our product execs (East Coast US) would prefer a morning slot (roughly 09:30–11:00 EST), our EU engineering team (based in Berlin) is only available late in their day (roughly 16:00–18:00 CET), and we may have an APAC observer (India) who can do early evening IST (after 20:00 IST).

We realize this is a squeeze across zones — ideally we want a single 60-minute demo where the core technical Q&A can include the EU engineers. Short of that, we can do a split (60m for execs + 30m technical follow-up) but prefer to avoid two full sessions if possible.

Can you propose concrete windows with explicit local times? There's been some confusion internally around DST cutovers, so if you can include UTC conversions that will help schedule with our calendar admin. I attached a short doc with our requirements.

Thanks,

Hi Emily — great notes, thank you. Copying Marissa (SE) and Soojin (EMEA) so we can propose technically feasible windows and make sure an engineer can present.

Two practical approaches that usually work:

Option A — single session (preferred): pick a UTC time that sits in the US morning and EU late afternoon. For example:
- 15:00 UTC / 10:00 EST (US execs) / 16:00 CET (EU engineers) / 20:30 IST (India)
This puts the EU team in their late afternoon and the US execs in mid-morning; the APAC attendee would be in the evening.

Option B — split session: a 45–60m exec-facing demo in US morning + a 30–45m technical deep-dive later for EU engineers. We can record the exec session and make the recording available before the technical follow-up.

Notes:
- We'll include UTC conversions in the invite to avoid DST confusion.
- If the APAC observer is only joining for a portion, we can record a short focused recap to send.

Marissa — can you check availability for an EMEA engineer to present at 15:00 UTC next Tue/Wed? Soojin, any calendar conflicts on your side for week of Dec 21?
